I have 10.1 mu. I keep about 8 mu for wheat-maize like always, and 2.1 mu for cotton. My father planted cotton, I planted cotton my whole life, the dealer in town still buys it, so I keep that piece. My son works in Handan now, so it is me and my wife most of the year. We hire the combine at harvest, everything else we do ourselves.

**Wheat (winter, 8 mu):** I plant after October 10, like every year. I use improved wheat seed from the agri-station — Jimai or whatever they have, the neighbors all buy the same. Before planting I spread 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu, that is 100 jin of 15-15-15. In spring when I turn the water on, I put 1 bag of urea per mu for topdressing, about 40 jin. Water four times — before winter, returning green, jointing, filling. Spray three times — one for weeds in spring, one for aphids and powdery mildew, one mixed spray at filling for one-spray-three-prevention. Rotary till before seeding because maize straw needs to be chopped in. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu, I expect the same.

**Maize (summer, 8 mu):** Right after wheat harvest I direct-seed maize, no ploughing, just drill into the stubble. Everyone does it this way now, saves two days. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu, whatever my input dealer pushes — I trust him, he is my wife's cousin. Basal 1 bag of compound per mu when seeding, then at big trumpet stage 1 bag of urea. Water once or twice if the rain is short in July-August, the well is there if needed. Spray for armyworm and aphids, maybe twice. I usually get 1100 jin per mu.

**Cotton (spring-autumn, 2.1 mu):** I plough this piece properly in April, cotton needs loose soil. Bt hybrid seed, the bollworm problem is smaller now but aphids and mirids still come. 1 bag compound before planting, half a bag of urea at budding, and I add some potassium because my old land is tired — maybe 20 jin of potassium per mu extra. Water three times if the summer is dry. I still spray six times or so — cotton needs watching, I walk the rows every few days. Yield maybe 450 jin of seed cotton per mu, cotton is not what it used to be but the price is okay.

I do not change much year to year. What worked last year will work this year. Fertilizer is expensive but losing the crop is worse, so I put on enough.
